title: Usha Devi v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
coram: Krishna Murari, J. & Ashwani Kumar Mishra, J.
disposition: Writ petition disposed of with liberty to apply for instalments under Clause 6.14, the authority to decide sympathetically within three weeks; no coercive steps for two months
headnote: Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 itself provides for payment of outstanding dues in easy instalments to consumers in financial distress (the Executive Engineer / DGM / General Manager granting up to two/three/four monthly instalments, the first not below 40% of the total). A residential consumer unable, due to financial distress, to pay dues of Rs. 1,37,472 was relegated to this remedy: the Court directed her to apply under Clause 6.14 within three weeks, the appropriate authority to decide sympathetically by a speaking order within a further three weeks, and stayed coercive recovery for two months or until disposal.

holding_units.topic: Easy-instalment facility for a residential consumer in financial distress
holding_units.question: Can a consumer in financial distress be relegated to the Clause 6.14 instalment mechanism rather than a mandamus fixing instalments?
holding_units.holding: Yes. Clause 6.14 provides for payment of outstanding dues in instalments to consumers in financial distress (no waiver of surcharge; the first instalment not below 40%). The consumer was directed to apply under Clause 6.14 within three weeks, the appropriate authority to decide sympathetically by a speaking and reasoned order within a further three weeks, with no coercive recovery for two months or until disposal.
holding_units.limiting_facts: Residential connection; dues of Rs. 1,37,472; financial distress; recovery proceedings initiated.

principle_tags.application: A consumer in financial distress is entitled to seek easy instalments under Clause 6.14, to be decided sympathetically, with interim protection from coercive recovery.
